findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The hand sink is observed to have a very loose faucet. Ensure this item is reattached to create a secure seal for the faucet attached to the sink basin.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: Observed multiple employees go from one task to another without washing their hands after contamination occurs. Inspector had a discussion with the PIC about hand washing and to ensure retraining and education are given to their staff regarding hand washing. Ensure hand washing is completed to ensure contamination does not occur of the food being handled.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: The hand sink was observed to have multiple rags in the basin which inhibited employees form accessing the hand sink. These rags were removed immediately and education was provided to the PIC as to why having the hand sink clear is crucial to contamination prevention. Ensure this hand sink remains clear and is only used for hand washing.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The sanitizer bucket was observed to have been used with soap as there were many bubbles present. It was confirmed by the employees that soap was indeed mistakingly used instead of bleach. This bucket was immediately dumped and filled with fresh warm water and bleach at a concentration of 100ppm. Ensure the sanitizer bucket is at least 100ppm bleach to be used for sanitizing the kitchen surfaces.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Many areas in the kitchen, including, but not limited to the shelves and under hard to reach areas, are observed to be in need of a detailed cleaning. Ensure detailed cleaning is performed at a frequency necessary to prevent the accumulation of soil residues.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: The shelving units int he back of the facility are observed to have missing or shipped paint which has exposed bare wood. THis bare wood needs to be resealed by using a sealant such  as paint to make the surface smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable.
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: In the walk-in cooler, raw chicken was observed to be stored in a container above cooked fried rice. The chicken was moved during the inspection to prevent the potential contamination of the rice. Ensure proper storage practices are followed to ensure the safety and the integrity of the food remains.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The bleach sanitizer bucket registered at a level below 50ppm when tested. Bleach was added to the solution during the inspection and registered at 100-200ppm. Ensure that the test strips are regularly utilized to ensure the sanitizer concentration is sufficient enough to accomplish the sanitization process.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: There were observed multiple wiping cloths on the counter being used to wipe off surfaces and then stored on the counter surface. These rags were placed into the corrected sanitizer solution during the inspection. Ensure the rags are placed into the sanitizer solution between uses to prevent cross contamination from the rag’s surface to the object being cleaned and sanitized.
3-304.14: (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: Multiple surfaces in the facility are in need of a general cleaning. These surfaces include the floor, wall, and shelving. Ensure these items are cleaned at a frequency to prevent soil and residue accumulation and the deter the presence of pests.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: When the inspector went to wash their hands, it was noted that there were no paper towels available. During the hand washing, a roll of paper towels was brought to the inspector. Ensure that the hand sink is always supplied with soap, paper towels, and a trash can nearby.
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: It was observed during the start of the inspection that there was no sanitizer bucket made and ready to use. Inspector provided education to the facility that during any hours of operation or during any prep work there must be a sanitizer bucket available with 100-200ppm of bleach. The sanitizer bucket was created during the time of the inspection and recorded using test strips to be between 100-200ppm bleach solution.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10).

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: It was observed that the tongs in the prep table were stored with the handles touching the foods. This action was corrected by the inspector on sight and reeducating the staff was performed by the PIC on how to properly store the in use utensils to prevent contamination.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
1) 5-204.11 A HANDWASHING SINK shall be located: (A) To allow convenient use by EMPLOYEES in FOOD preparation, FOOD dispensing, and WAREWASHING areas (B) In, or immediately adjacent to, toilet rooms. On arrival, the hand sink at the back of the kitchen was difficult o reach due to a barrel being in the way with a container of food on top. Inspector moved the barrel to facilitate their own hand washing during the inspection. 
2) 6-301.12 Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with:
(A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. The men's bathroom was without paper towels during the inspection. The PIC stated that they ran out of the ones intended for the dispenser and had been drying their hands elsewhere. Inspector stated that all hand sinks need to be supplied adequately to facilitate hand washing. A roll of paper towels was provided during the inspection.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  (P) A bucket of "sweet n sour" sauce is observed under the end of the three part sink and to have floating particles on the surface. The sauce was discarded during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
1) 3-305.12  (C) Food may not be stored in: 1) locker rooms; 2) toilet rooms; 3) dressing rooms; 4) garbage rooms; 5) mechanical rooms; 6) under non shielded sewer lines; 7) under leaking water lines; 8) under open stairwells; 9) under other sources of contamination. "Sweet n sour" sauce and soaking vegetables are observed stored under the 3 part sink. This is not a safe location to store containers of food. 
2) 3-305.11  (C) Food shall be protected by contamination by storing it: 1) in a clean, dry location; 2) where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination; 3) at least 6 inches above the floor. A container of cooked beef in the walk in cooler ia observed without a covering. PIC is instructed to ensure that all foods are adequately protected from contamination.

findings.citation_text: 2-103.11 (P) The Person in Charge shall ensure that: (O) “Food Employees and Conditional Employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as relate to disease that are transmissible through food as specified under 2-201.11 (A). findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Food contact surfaces should be washed, rinsed and sanitized often enough so as to be maintained clean. The blade of the can opener was observed heavily soiled during the inspection. The can opener was moved to the 3 part sink for cleaning.

findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text:
750.540 (C) The food establishment is not under the operational supervision of a Certified Food Service Sanitation Manager that is present at appropriate times. Provide an adequate number of staff with approved training. Reference 750.540.

Observed no CFM upon entering facility for complaint. CFM was called in order to answer questions regarding the complaint. Ensure a CFM is at facility during all hours of operation. CFM training paperwork was left with the PIC in order to assure no future violations occur.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on multiple food items within walk-in cooler. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

Observed several items within walk-in cooler to lack date marking including raw beef and chicken. PIC stated that these items were just prepped. PIC had food handlers cover items with syran wrap and date marking. Date marking was discussed with PIC and stressed importance of maintaining procedure throughout prep time. COS.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

Observed multiple items in facility to have no syran wrap covering items. Walk-in: raw beef and raw chicken. Bottom prep cooler: raw chicken and imitation crab sticks. Discussed having all food items covered within walk-in and bottom prep cooler in order to protect against contamination. COS.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animalfoods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

Observed in-use wiping clothes on counter near prep area. In-use wiping clothes were not stored in sanitization solution bucket. Ensure all in-use wiping clothes are held within a sani bucket at all times with appropriate concentrations of sanitizer.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16  (C) Mop was found stored incorrectly in-between use. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies.  Reference 6-501.16.

Observed mop to be stored in-between uses in a manner that does not allow for drip drying and/or air drying. Ensure mops are stored in a manner for proper air drying such as upside down.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
Observed raw shrimp thawing in standing water in the three compartment sink. Shrimp was probed at 70F. Cold water was started, and shrimp was taken to be peeled shortly after. 

Raw meat that had been cut at the beginning of the inspection was also observed thawing at room temperature on the speed cart. Thawing was discussed. Meat must be frozen to the chopped and then must thaw in order to add the flour mixture. PIC states that raw meat will be prepared after prep employees are finished with the shrimp.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13  (C) Time and temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be thawed: (A) Under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41°F or less; or (B) Completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70°F or below, with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and for a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of ready-to-eat food to rise above 41°F; or (C) As part of a cooking process; or (D) Using any procedure if a portion of frozen ready-to-eat food is thawed and prepared for immediate service in response to an individual consumer's order. Reference 3-501.13.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Observed personal foods stored intermingled with food for the public in both the reach in freezer (foods and bowls stored in the door) and in the walk in cooler (chicken for personal use stored above foods for the public). All personal foods should be labeled and stored in a manner that does not have the potential to contaminate food for the public (below and in separate areas). 

Observed open cans of ketchup and pineapple in the bottom of the prep cooler. Once cans of acidic foods are opened, food should be transferred to a food grade container.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11. -

Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.citation_text: 2-102.11(A) (Pf) PIC did not demonstrate sufficient knowledge. Discussed related section of the food code.  Reference 2-102.11(A).

findings.comment:

Final cooking temperatures were discussed with the PIC in relation to storage in coolers. In the process of moving this ground beef, the juices spilled on a box of broccoli. Box of broccoli was voluntarily discarded.

findings.citation_text: 3-302.11  (P)  Store raw animal products below ready to eat foods so they are separate and protected from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized

There were numerous knives on the magnetic strip that were soiled as well as a whole pan of utensils stored on a bottom shelf that had visible food remnants on them (appeared to be raw meat remnants). findings.citation_text: 4-501.114  (P) Provide 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration. Reference 4-501.114.

findings.title: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures & records
findings.comment: Observed garlic in oil on the cook line that was reported to have been put there this morning to be probed at an internal temperature of 77F with no indication marked as to when this was removed from cold holding. A time as a control policy will need to be completed (completed during the inspection) for the house made sauces and garlic in oil mixture that is kept at ambient air throughout the day. The time needs to be marked when these are removed from cold holding and any left at the end of 4 hours will need to be discarded.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.19  (P) When a maximum time period of 4 hours is used for food safety, TCS food must have an initial temperature of 41°F or less when removed from cold holding temperature control, or 135°F or greater when removed from hot holding temperature control. Discussed the HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.19.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: Observed numerous items in the cooling process in the facility such as chicken, rice and steamed broccoli. Chicken at the front prep table near the fryer was probed at 76F and was reported to have been cooked at 11:30 am. Rice in the walk in cooler was in a large bowl with a smaller bowl within and was probed at 119F after being cooked at 12:30pm. Chicken that is being cooked and cooled is in large heaps on the tray rack and probed at 195F. It is hard to have a clear understanding if these items are cooling properly because no time or temperatures are being written down. Most of these items are cooked well above 165F and cooled at room temperature in large batches before being placed in the walk in cooler eventually. Cooling should be done in small batches, single layers uncovered and rapidly so that foods reach 70F within the first 2 hours of the cooling process. It is unknown if this is occurring or not since foods are inadvertently being hot held for some time before they cool from cooking temperature to 135F. 3-501.15  (Pf) To cool rapidly, use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

Food in the walk-in cooler was observed to be cooling in large quantities in single containers and in covered containers.

Put accurate thermometers in the units mentioned above.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750.140b - Multiple cooked and raw foods stored in walkin cooler and walkin freezer were not properly labeled. Label all foods with dates and time of prep and include the common names of foods that are not easily identifiable. Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F/below.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - Fried rice sitting out by wok grill was 76F. Rice was discarded in the trash. Potentially hazardous foods shall be maintained at 41F/below. Do not pull foods from cold holding and leave them sitting out for long periods of time. Get food out in portions as needed. A time control policy must be established and adhered to if employees and management want to leave working supplies of PHF sitting out for use during busy operating hours.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750.130d - (x2) A) Raw meat was stored over cooked egg rolls and cooked noodles on a roll cart. Trays of food were rearranged so all raw products were below ready to eat foods. B) Raw chicken was observed over a container of sprouts in the walking cooler. Proper raw food storage was discussed and foods were rearranged in walkin cooler so raw products were not directly over ready to eat foods. All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or away from raw foods. Store raw meats properly in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - A) (R)  Bags of potato starch, sugar, and flour were observed on the floor in dry storage area. Store foods up off the floor at least 6 inches. B) Open #10 cans of ketchup and pineapple were observed in the walkin cooler and bottom holding area of prep cooler on the cook line. Store acidic foods in proper food grade re-usable containers after original cans are opened. Leaving acidic foods in original cans after opening can cause metals/metallic flavor to leak into foods.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text: 750.160 - (R) Cup was observed being used as a scoop in a container of potato starch. Cup was removed/discarded. Use scoops with handles for dispensing foods to avoid direct hand contact.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.

Use paper towels, parchment paper, or another material suitable for soaking up grease. Discard the paper towels or parchment paper after each use. Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Dishwashing facilities designed, constructed, operated (1. wash 2. rinse 3. sanitize)
findings.citation_text: 750.820 - (R) Three part sink was not setup to allow for proper manual wash, rinse, and sanitize. Employee was observed rinsing off a knife and scrubbing it with a sponge at the middle compartment of the 3 part sink. Knife was then placed back by food prep area for use.  Proper wash, rinse, sanitize and setup of 3 part sink was discussed with employees. Employees were advised on cleaning and sanitizing sinks prior to setting up 3 part sink for ware washing.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750.830g - Chlorine test strips were not available for checking sanitizer concentrations. Obtain and use chlorine test strips. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million. (3 part sink = 50ppm chlorine & sanitizer buckets = 100ppm chlorine).

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment: 750.820a - (R) Employee was observed rinsing off a knife and scrubbing it with a sponge at the middle compartment of the 3 part sink. Have 3 part sink setup for proper ware washing prior to beginning process, and maintain the drain board in a clean sanitary manner. (sanitizer in sink=50ppm chlorine; bucket=100ppm chlorine) Proper wash, rinse, sanitize and setup of 3 part sink was discussed with employees. Employees were advised on cleaning and sanitizing sinks prior to setting up 3 part sink for ware washing.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - A) (R) A sanitizer bucket was not setup for wiping general surfaces at the front counter. B) Wet wiping cloths were observed on the front counter upon arrival of inspectors. Maintain buckets of sanitizer solution for wiping general surfaces. Have a separate sanitizer bucket setup for sanitizing clean in place food contact surfaces. Store wiping cloths in solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms. Sanitizer solutions in buckets must be maintained at 100ppm chlorine. **Solution was made during the inspection.**

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled: A) (R) cleaver storage rack (food debris/general splash); B) cleavers & knives in storage rack; C) soiled colanders on shelf above 3part sink; D) can opener blade (heavy buildup of food debris); E) hood and filters above cook line; F) soiled container and tongs by rice cooker by front counter; & G) knife that was observed not properly cleaned and sanitized (see #20a). Properly clean and sanitize all food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of food and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750.800e -The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled: A) (R) general surfaces of roll cart storing baking sheets (food debris/splash); B) (R) outside of metal cans used for rice storage (sticky buildup); C) the metal rack holding rice cans; D) top of char-broiler and attached pipe (grease/dust); E) general surfaces of cooking equipment; F) inside fryer panels around mechanicals; G) shelves in walkin cooler; & H) black storage racks in walkin freezer. Clean all non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.citation_text: 750.860 - A) Clean baking sheets were observed stored on the floor between the ice machine and the wall.  Store cleaned and sanitized equipment up off the floor at least 6 inches to protect items from potential contamination. Baking sheets were moved off the floor. B) Soiled colanders were observed stored on top of clean colanders on shelf above the 3 part sink. Store soiled equipment separate from clean equipment so avoid cross contamination. Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be stored and handled in a way that protects them from contamination.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.citation_text: 750.1060 - What appeared to be grease was observed around the top of the grease trap. Unsure as to whether grease was coming out of the top of the trap. An employee stated the grease trap gets cleaned once every 3 months, and the employee is the person who cleans it. Staff were advised a licensed septic pumper must pump and clean the grease trap. This is a special waste and must be disposed of properly. Hire a licensed professional to properly clean the grease trap. All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 - Floors were soiled throughout the facility, especially in the following areas: A) along the wall between flour storage and the walkin freezer; B) along the wall below the 3 part sink; C) around and on top of the grease trap; D) under and behind the smoker, fryers, and wok line; & E) under shelves in freezer. Clean the floors throughout and maintain them clean.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 - Walls throughout facility and all attached equipment, such as the underside of the 3 part sink, and plumbing were observed to be soiled with food debris, splash, and general buildup. Thoroughly clean the walls, the undersides of the 3 part sink and other attached equipment and plumbing throughout the facility.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text: 750.1280 - (R) Employee cell phones and other personal items were observed stored intermixed with single service items and food. An adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from all food, food related items, and food prep/storage areas to reduce the potential for cross contamination. Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.citation_text: 750.1350 - Garbage, an unused storage container, and a broken fryer were being stored in the back hallway. Food service establishments and all parts of property used in connection with their operation shall be kept free of litter and garbage. Only articles necessary for the operation and maintenance of the food service establishment shall be stored on the premises.  Remove all unnecessary items and properly dispose of garbage. Do not store garbage in the back hallway.

findings.title: No Certified Manager Present
findings.comment: 750.540a - (R) Certified food handler was not on-site upon arrival of the inspectors. Employee stated it was manager's day off but an employee was going to call him to come in for the inspection. An employee later stated the manager was at a doctor appointment. The manager is the only certified food handler currently employed at the facility. Manager was advised at the July routine inspection that more certified food handlers need to be hired/trained. All Category I facilities must employ an adequate number of  Licensed Food Service Sanitation Managers to have one present at all times food is being prepared to help ensure proper food handling.  Provide an adequate number of  Food Service Sanitation Manager. **FSSMC arrived at end of inspection. Violation considered remaining because more food handlers need to be hired**

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.citation_text: 750.100 - Multiple dented cans of vegetables were observed in dry storage area. All cans were separated from cans that were in good condition. Damaged cans were also labeled in Mandarin so employees would know the cans of food could not be used. findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text: 750.130 & 140 - A) Cooking wine in clear bottle in the bottom of prep cooler was not labeled. Label was placed on the bottle. Bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name. B) Cooling rice in the walkin cooler did not have the date and time on it. PHF shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - (x2) A) Beef, pork, and chicken in the top holding area of the prep cooler were 48F-60F. All foods were discarded in the trash during the inspection. Prep cooler was holding at 41F/below, and all foods in the bottom were at proper temperature. Keep lids on containers of food between uses/keep the large lid of the prep cooler closed during slow periods to help maintain colder temperatures. B) Eggrolls on a plate by the fryers were 84F. Eggrolls were discarded in the trash. Eggrolls were placed out during lunch to fry as needed. Maintain cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) at 41F/below or use time control for cold PHF that is pulled out and held at room temperature during busy periods.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.citation_text: 750.140(b) - (x2) A) Chicken in plastic tub in upright cooler by the front counter was at 65F-87F. Employee stated it had been fried at 11am today. Product was just placed in walkin cooler according to employee. Rice was separated into smaller portions in colanders to speed up the cooling process. Cooked PHF shall be properly cooled from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in an additional 4 hours (total cooling time must not exceed 6 hours).

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage

Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination. Maintain ice scoop and inside the ice machine clean to protect ice from potential cross contamination.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text: 750.160 - (x2) A) Fried chips were stored inside a cardboard box which previously contained sleeves of single service cups. Chips were moved to a tupperware container. findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text: 750.160 - Cup was observed being used as a scoop in a container of white powder. Cup was removed/discarded. Use scoops with handles for dispensing foods to avoid direct hand contact.

findings.citation_text: 750.130 - Raw foods (beef & chicken) were stored above containers of vegetables & sauces in the walkin cooler. Also, raw chicken was observed above raw beef in walkin cooler. Never store raw foods above ready to eat foods in coolers or freezers. Always store raw meats in the order of their cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature product on the bottom (raw chicken must always be below all other raw meats, raw beef & pork must be above raw chicken, and raw seafood must be above all other raw meats). Always store ready to eat foods separate from/above raw foods. Foods were placed in proper storage order in the walkin cooler during the inspection.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 750.120 - A) Foods in coolers and other locations were uncovered (egg rolls & vegetables in walkin cooler; various foods in prep cooler)/left out over night (dirty pan with flour in it). Keep foods covered when they are not being used, and always cover foods at the end of the business day before you leave for night. Do not leave containers of foods uncovered over night. Flour was discarded in trash, and dirty container was placed at 3 compartment sink to be cleaned/sanitized. B) Tomato sauce was left in open can in prep cooler over night. Place leftover tomato paste in reusable plastic container at the end of the day. Don't store acidic foods in metal cans after they are opened (metals can leak in to food & rust may form)
